edbDesc: The Lagrangian points are the five positions in an orbital configuration where a small object affected only by gravity can theoretically be stationary relative to two larger objects (such as a satellite with respect to the Earth and Moon). The Lagrange points mark positions where the combined gravitational pull of the two large masses provides precisely the centripetal force required to rotate with them.
title: Lagrangian points
description: Around any two orbiting bodies, like the Sun and Earth, there are five spots where a small object's pulls balance so it keeps pace with them. Joseph-Louis Lagrange found them in 1772 in Berlin (Euler had found three). Space telescopes park there for a steady view with little fuel.
effect: a small body stays put relative to two big orbiting bodies at five balance points
usedIn: James Webb Space Telescope at Sun-Earth L2
strength: Sun-Earth L1 and L2 lie 1.5 million km from Earth; a craft there needs only a few metres per second of thrust a year to stay.
pickWhy: Not in the deck: trojan-asteroids (1906) confirmed it but is a later discovery by a different person; algebra-and-mechanics is Lagrange's different 1788 work.
